summary.title: Part 3 - Designing our Frontend
summary.one_liner: You learn how to split a React frontend into components (a Header function component and a ChatHistory class component) and feed WebSocket messages from a Go backend into component state.
keywords: how to render list of messages in react
takeaways: React apps are divided into components, each in its own directory with a .jsx file, a .scss file and an index.js export.
A simple function component (Header) can be created and imported into App.js to render at the top of the page.
A class component (ChatHistory) receives an array of messages via props and renders each one in its render() method.
The WebSocket connect() function is extended with a callback that fires on each incoming message.
App.js holds chatHistory in state, initialised in the constructor, and updates it via setState in componentDidMount.
summary.summary: This is part 3 of a series building a realtime chat app with a Go WebSocket backend and a ReactJS frontend. The article walks through creating a Header function component and a ChatHistory class component, each with its own folder, SCSS styling and index.js export. It then updates the WebSocket api code to accept a callback on each incoming message and wires that callback into App.js state so received messages render in the chat history. The post is hands-on code with step-by-step snippets.
